Is there a way to keep your hands from drying out without using stupid lotion?
St. Ives lotion doesn't fail as a lotion. As compared to other lotions, it does a good job without leaving a soap scum feeling on your skin.

When you wash/shower, don't use very hot water, avoid strong soaps/detergents and don't scrub them dry with a towel. All of those things strip the natural oil from your skin.

Coconut and olive oils are reasonable a replacement/supplement for natural skin oil. A lot of commercial lotions are actually petroleum bi-products that treat some symptoms of dry skin but are mostly just a way for oil barons to make an extra buck.

Last year I had a sunburn and spent some time reading the labels of the various treatments available at Walmart. The one I settled on was called Ocean Potion and it turned out to be generally pretty good for skin apart from burns too. It didn't have alcohol (which is evaporative/drying) but it did have all kinds of balms/nutrients including aloe, vitamin E, seaweed, etc. If you find some and try it, be careful because it's also got tea tree oil, which is mildly camphorous/tingly/stingy/spicy (but also functions as a topical antibiotic against germs).

Make sure you drink enough water. A good way to get in the habit and develop a sense for what it feels like to be well hydrated is to do the gallon-a-day challenge for a couple weeks.
